In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the postswitch alternative does have some influence on behavior, that influence is indirect and is probably due to the different relative distributions of reinforcement that are obtained when different postswitch alternatives are signaled.

the results of the present experiment show that, although the postswitch alternative does influence choice, it does so in an indirect and subtle way, and the main effects of alternation arrangements can be accounted for by the relative reinforcement rates of the different schedules.
pigeons respond to signaled and unsignaled random alternation in the same way, but the postswitch alternative is a factor that affects behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

pigeons respond as though they were maximizing the rate of reinforcement, but that they do this by maximizing the distribution of reinforcers across time, and that the distribution is influenced by the relative rates of reinforcement and by the postswitch alternatives. , although behavior in a variable-interval concurrent schedule is sensitive to the postswitch alternative when that alternative is signaled and when it is unsignaled, the mechanism is the same in both cases.
, in the absence of a signal, the postswitch alternative does not affect behavior, and in the presence of a signal, it does, but only through its effects on the distribution of reinforcers
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when random alternation is arranged, pigeons are able to respond in a sensitive manner to the relative reinforcement of alternatives.

the effects of signaling the postswitch alternative are not due to a simple bias in choice, but rather to the indirect effects of the distributions of reinforcer ratios between alternatives obtained prior to that alternative.

pigeons are sensitive to the relative reinforcement rates of alternatives, even when they have no direct access to that information, and that the pigeon is a useful model for studying the mechanisms of choice.
